reconcile.note: Matthew Henry ranks the two: Levitical blood atoned only figuratively, as an imperfect type, while true atonement belongs to Christ's blood alone.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll challenges the whole Mosaic blood-atonement scheme the Levitical law affirms, asking how the shedding of an animal's blood could ever atone for a man's sin.

quotes.text: Under the Mosaic dispensation, there was no remission of sin except through the shedding of blood. … The priest would lay his hands upon the animal, and the sin of the man would be transferred. Then the animal would be killed in the place of the real sinner, and the blood thus shed and sprinkled upon the altar would be an atonement.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III, Ingersoll's Rejoinder to Judge Jeremiah S. Black (1881), on Leviticus 17:11.

sides.snippet: it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
sides.verseText: For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.

sides.snippet: it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
sides.verseText: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
